↓ Download CV

Pedro writes letters he never sends, paints abstract pieces, and pretends he's a musician. Photography and video are his favourite ways to tell stories.

Born in Porto, based between London and Porto. Multidisciplinary artist and creative professional with international experience across photography, curation, event production, and art direction.

His work is experimental, emotional, and deeply personal — always evolving. His practice isn't about having it all figured out; it's about the journey, the questions, and the messy, beautiful process of creating.

2022 — Photography — Personal

I Would Rather Not
Go Back To The Old House

A story of failed love told through six photographs, each one a chapter. The sequence follows the Rider-Waite tarot — not as mysticism, but as a borrowed language for emotions that resist ordinary words.

click anywhere to begin →

0

The Fool

The Fool is me. Numbered zero — the beginning of everything, or the end. He stands at the cliff's edge with a flower in his hand. Too new to know fear. But look closely at his gaze: it is already downward. Not at the ground — more like something inside him already knows. The naivety of beginning something, and underneath it, a quiet shadow.

III

The Empress

Feminine, abundant, present in every sense. Look at her hand — extended outward, open, offering. She is available, interested, reaching toward something. This is how it began: the gesture of someone who seems to be waiting for someone to take what they are offering. And I took it.

VI

The Lovers

Look at where each figure stands. The Fool is below — smaller, reaching upward. The Empress stands above, elevated. This is the power dynamic the card never says out loud. He looks at her hand, the same hand she offered. She doesn't look at him. Her gaze is elsewhere.

XIII

Death

Death is the funeral. Not a metaphor — the actual burial of something that was real. People say Death in tarot means transformation, not ending. Maybe. But you still have to stand there and watch it happen. You still have to be at the funeral before anything can begin again.

XII

The Hanged Man

This is where I lived for a while. Suspended — bound, hanging, unable to move forward or return. I couldn't breathe. I couldn't move. I felt broken and stuck in time. Not grief exactly. Closer to asphyxiation. You are still alive, which is almost the worst part.

XVIII

The Moon

The Moon is the only thing in the sky you cannot touch. I understand that now. She will always be my moon — I can see her from here, I can love her from here, but I will never hold her. That is the final stage: arriving at a kind of peace with the distance.
